name: Mutters
kurzbeschreibung: Vacation spot in the Mittelgebirge with the Mutterer Alm, Mutterer Höhe, and the famous Pfarrkirche with its onion-shaped tower.
text:
Overview

Mutters is situated on a sun-drenched plateau of the southern Mittelgebirge at an altitude of 848 meters, approximately six kilometers southwest of Innsbruck, the provincial capital of Tyrol. Located in the Innsbruck-Land district, the municipality has around 2,250 residents and includes the scenic hamlets of Kreith and Raitis alongside the main village. Thanks to its elevated terrace setting, Mutters boasts sweeping panoramic views across the rugged Nordkette range, the Inn valley floor, and the dramatic limestone cone of the Serles. The village's local mountain is the 1,620-meter Muttereralm, a year-round recreational wonderland. Mutters combines traditional Tyrolean rural charm with instant access to Innsbruck's urban cultural life.

History

Archaeological discoveries of Bronze Age tools and urn graves demonstrate that human settlement on the Mutters terrace dates back more than 3,000 years. The earliest written documentation appears between 1115 and 1124 under the name 'Muttres', derived from the Rhaeto-Romanic word 'mutta' signifying a rounded hill or knoll. Mutters acquired national historic fame during the Tyrolean Rebellion of 1809. Tyrolean freedom fighter Andreas Hofer set up his military headquarters at the historic Gasthof Schupfen, coordinating the decisive Battles of Bergisel against Napoleonic Bavarian and French forces from here. The spiritual centerpiece of the village is the parish church of St. Nicholas (St. Nikolaus), featuring late Gothic roots, a classic onion-domed steeple, and frescoes by Anton Zoller. Since 1904, the iconic Stubaitalbahn tram has connected Mutters directly with Innsbruck.

Getting There

Mutters boasts exceptional accessibility and one of Austria's most scenic public transit approaches. By car from Innsbruck, drivers take the A13 Brenner Autobahn to exit Innsbruck-Süd/Mutters, or take the toll-free country road via Natters, reaching the village in under ten minutes. By public transport, the Stubaitalbahn (line STB) narrow-gauge railway provides a charming travel experience: boarding in front of Innsbruck Hauptbahnhof, the panoramic tram winds past alpine meadows and woodlands straight to Mutters and onward to Kreith in approximately 30 minutes. Regular VVT regional buses also connect the village with Innsbruck.

Tips

The modern Muttereralmbahn cable car carries hikers, mountain bikers, and sightseers directly up to the alpine adventure zone of the Muttereralm. Next to the scenic reservoir lake, children explore the 'Zauberwasser' (Magic Water) adventure playground complete with wooden sluices and sensory stations. Thrill-seekers flock to Bikepark Innsbruck, which features world-renowned downhill trails that host the international Crankworx mountain bike festival. A highlight for the whole family is descending the five-kilometer mountain cart track back to the valley. History buffs should visit Gasthof Schupfen to view the preserved Andreas Hofer memorial room from 1809. In winter, the mountain becomes a family ski resort featuring groomed pistes and illuminated tobogganing.
